evidence: src/infrastructure/inMemoryRepositories.ts: InMemoryUserRepository, InMemoryProjectRepository and InMemoryTaskRepository implement the domain interfaces UserRepository, ProjectRepository and TaskRepository (persistence adapters)

src/infrastructure/app.ts: createApp(service?: TaskManagementService) wires the Express routes, and every handler calls svc.* methods only; the in-memory repositories appear only in the default construction of TaskManagementService
src/infrastructure/server.ts: the only statement is createApp().listen(port, ...), so it is purely the startup entry point
src/infrastructure/app.ts: the status check uses the domain's isTaskStatus in both handlers, but the message 'status must be todo, in_progress or done' is written out twice (minor)
src/infrastructure/app.ts: GET /projects/:projectId/tasks checks assigneeId with an inline typeof test instead of the module's str() helper (minor inconsistency)
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The three files form one cohesive infrastructure concern: adapting the application to the outside world. src/infrastructure/inMemoryRepositories.ts holds the persistence adapters, which implement the domain repository interfaces. src/infrastructure/app.ts holds the HTTP adapter (createApp, Express routes, and error-to-status mapping via DomainError.code). src/infrastructure/server.ts is the startup entry point that calls createApp().listen. Every route handler in app.ts goes through the TaskManagementService facade (svc.createUser, svc.createTask, svc.listTasks, svc.assignTask, svc.markDone) and none touches the repositories directly; the repositories appear only in createApp's default service construction. The status rule lives in the domain's isTaskStatus, and filter logic lives once in InMemoryTaskRepository.findByProject. There are two minor inconsistencies in app.ts. First, the message 'status must be todo, in_progress or done' is written out in both the POST and GET task handlers, though the check itself is not duplicated. Second, the GET handler checks assigneeId with an inline typeof test instead of the module's str() helper. Neither is a split concern, a duplicated invariant, or a bypass of a module abstraction, so the module passes.
